description: The roles of an anaesthetic record, written with no hospital in mind. A hospital's map supplies each role view as one SELECT over its own tables, and an audit written against the role views then runs unchanged at any hospital. roles.md, beside this file, explains each role in words.
versioning: Version 1 of the contract is the three views whose status is contract, which the audits read, and their columns are unchanged since 1.0. Version 1.1 adds beside them the mapping views, the source kinds and the capability catalogue, and reshapes the draft parts. A view whose status is draft is not yet used by any audit, and its columns may still change.
rules: One row of role_anaesthetic is one anaesthetic, and its key identifies that anaesthetic and no other.

A view gives each time as the source holds it, without conversion, and the hospital schema records the time zone that the source's clocks follow and whether the source applies daylight saving; an audit that needs an elapsed time across a change of daylight saving must say so.
A reading, an event, a drug given, a device, a fluid or a person present belongs to an anaesthetic by its link to that anaesthetic, and never because its time falls within the anaesthetic.
A laboratory result and a diagnosis belong to the patient and the stay, and an audit that wants those near an anaesthetic chooses its own window around it.
A note belongs to an anaesthetic by its link to that anaesthetic where the hospital's system makes one, and otherwise to the stay or to the patient.
A role view keeps the rows that an audit leaves out, such as test patients, anaesthetics with no stop and values that were not accepted, so that the counts can see them.
A role view never joins in a way that repeats a row of the thing it describes, so that the view's key identifies its row.

A value that the record does not hold is empty, and a value that the record holds but that cannot be read as the role's type is also empty; role_reading then keeps the held text in value_text, so that the reason for an empty value can be counted.
A key compares equal with itself within one hospital only, and no key is carried from one hospital to another.

A value is in the unit that its role or its kind fixes, and a view converts a value held in another unit; only a drug's amount and a laboratory result of the kind other are given in the unit carried beside them.
A part that records events records each row as the source recorded it, with a key of its own, and never collapses rows that share a time or a kind, so that a question decides which to keep.
A part that records events marks each row with the kind of record it came from, from the source kind vocabulary, so that rows that reach the part by several pathways arrive marked.

Where a pathway's rows carry only the stay, the part's row carries stay_key and an empty anaesthetic_key, and a question attributes it to an anaesthetic by its own logic over the roles; the map never attributes a row by a time window.

A column that holds a code of an open domain, such as a drug, a procedure, a diagnosis, a laboratory test or a unit, holds the opaque local key of a mapping view and never the code; the code and its description stay in the hospital schema.

views.name: role_patient
views.title: Patients
views.description: One row for each patient, test and training patients included, so that an audit can leave them out.
views.holds: The patient table of the hospital's system, which holds one row for each person; the date of death is often held in a second patient table or loaded from a registry.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the patient, the same value that role_anaesthetic.patient_key holds.
columns.holds: The patient table's own key.

columns.name: birth_date
columns.title: date of birth
columns.meaning: The date of birth, to the day, so that an age in days counts calendar dates.
columns.holds: The patient table.

columns.name: death_date
columns.title: date of death
columns.meaning: The date of death where the hospital knows of it, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The patient table, a second patient table, or a table loaded from a death registry.

columns.name: is_test
columns.title: test patient
columns.meaning: 1 for a test or training patient who is not a real person, and 0 for every other patient.
columns.holds: A flag on the patient table or a second patient table, or a naming convention that the hospital uses for test patients.

views.name: role_anaesthetic
views.title: Anaesthetics
views.description: One row for each episode of anaesthesia or sedation given by an anaesthetist, including those whose start or stop is missing or out of order, so that the counts can see them.
views.holds: The anaesthetic record or anaesthesia episode, which is usually its own table, linked to a theatre case or to an encounter of its own.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the anaesthetic, the same value that role_reading.anaesthetic_key holds.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record's own key.
look_for: unique id of the anaesthesia episode

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient who had the anaesthetic, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the encounter or theatre case to which it is linked.

columns.name: start_time
columns.title: start time
columns.meaning: When the anaesthetic started, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the anaesthesia start event of the theatre case.

columns.name: stop_time
columns.title: stop time
columns.meaning: When the anaesthetic stopped, as the source holds it, and empty where no stop was recorded.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, or the anaesthesia stop event of the theatre case.

views.name: role_reading
views.title: Readings charted during an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each value charted in an anaesthetic's own record, with its kind from the vocabulary below, including values that were not accepted and values that are not numbers.
views.one_row_per: value charted in an anaesthetic's record
views.holds: A table of measurements or observations, often the largest in the system, with one row for each value of each kind at each moment, reached from the anaesthetic through the record or sheet on which it was charted.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic whose record holds the reading, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The sheet or record on which the reading was charted, which carries the anaesthetic's key or the key of the anaesthetic's own encounter.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of reading
columns.meaning: What was measured, as one of the kinds of the vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the reading that points at the system's own list of the things that can be charted.

columns.name: reading_time
columns.title: time of the reading
columns.meaning: When the value was taken, as the source holds it, and not when it was filed.
columns.holds: The reading itself, which often holds a second time at which the value was entered or received.

columns.name: value
columns.title: value
columns.meaning: The value as a number in the kind's own unit, and empty where the charted value is not a number.
columns.holds: The reading itself, usually as text that holds numbers and words alike.

columns.name: accepted
columns.title: accepted or rejected
columns.meaning: 1 where the value counts as valid, and 0 where it was marked as an artefact, rejected or superseded.
columns.holds: A flag on the reading, or the absence of the value after an edit, which the hospital's practice decides.

columns.name: reading_key
columns.title: the reading's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the charted value, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The reading's own key, which is often two columns, such as the sheet and the line on it.

columns.name: value_text
columns.title: the value as charted
columns.meaning: The value as the record holds it, where it cannot be read as a number, and empty where the value is a number or the record holds none.
columns.holds: The same column as the value, usually text that holds numbers and words alike.

views.name: role_patient_detail
views.title: The patient's details at birth
views.description: One row for each patient whose record holds any of these details, for the covariates of an audit.
views.holds: A second patient table, the birth history of the child, or the delivery record of the mother when it is linked to the baby.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The table that holds the details.

columns.name: sex
columns.title: sex at birth
columns.meaning: The sex recorded at birth, as one of the kinds of the sex vocabulary.
columns.holds: The patient table, usually as a code with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: gestation_weeks
columns.title: gestation in weeks
columns.meaning: The gestational age at birth in weeks, with any days as a fraction of a week.
columns.holds: The birth history, the newborn's delivery record, or a measurement charted on the newborn.

columns.name: birth_weight_grams
columns.title: birth weight in grams
columns.meaning: The weight at birth in grams.
columns.holds: The birth history, the newborn's delivery record, or a measurement charted on the newborn.

views.name: role_stay
views.title: Hospital stays
views.description: One row for each hospital stay, from admission to discharge, day stays included, for the length of stay and for readmission.
views.holds: The hospital encounter or admission table, which holds the admission and the discharge of each stay.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the stay, the same value that role_anaesthetic_detail.stay_key holds.
columns.holds: The encounter's own key.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient whose stay it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: admit_time
columns.title: admission time
columns.meaning: When the patient was admitted, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: discharge_time
columns.title: discharge time
columns.meaning: When the patient was discharged, or died in hospital, as the source holds it, and empty while the patient is still in hospital.
columns.holds: The encounter table.

columns.name: unplanned
columns.title: unplanned admission
columns.meaning: 1 for an emergency or other unplanned admission, 0 for a planned one, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The admission type or admission category of the encounter, as a code with a lookup table of names.

views.name: role_anaesthetic_detail
views.title: The anaesthetic's details
views.description: One row for each anaesthetic whose record holds any of these details, for the covariates and outcomes of an audit.
views.holds: Partly the anaesthetic record and partly the theatre case or surgical log, with the pre-anaesthetic assessment for the grade and the weight.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record's own key.
look_for: unique id of the anaesthesia episode

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay in which the anaesthetic took place, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty where the anaesthetic belongs to no stay.
columns.holds: The theatre case or the anaesthetic record, which points at the admission, sometimes through a link table.

columns.name: asa_grade
columns.title: ASA grade
columns.meaning: The ASA physical status grade from 1 to 6, without any letter for an emergency.
columns.holds: The pre-anaesthetic assessment, the anaesthetic record or the theatre case, usually as a code with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: is_emergency
columns.title: emergency operation
columns.meaning: 1 where the operation was done as an emergency, 0 where it was planned, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The theatre case or booking, or an E after the ASA grade.

columns.name: weight_kg
columns.title: weight in kilograms
columns.meaning: The patient's weight at the anaesthetic in kilograms.
columns.holds: The pre-anaesthetic assessment or a measurement charted on the day, and sometimes the theatre case.

columns.name: planned_icu
columns.title: planned intensive care
columns.meaning: 1 where intensive care after the operation was planned before it began, 0 where it was not, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The booking of the theatre case, as the planned destination after the operation or a request for an intensive care bed.

columns.name: unplanned_return
columns.title: unplanned return to theatre
columns.meaning: 1 where the operation was recorded as an unplanned return to theatre, 0 where it was not, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The theatre case, where the hospital records an unplanned return as a reason or a flag.

columns.name: height_cm
columns.title: height in centimetres
columns.meaning: The patient's height or length at the anaesthetic, in centimetres.
columns.holds: The pre-anaesthetic assessment or a measurement charted on the day, as the weight is.

columns.name: location
columns.title: location
columns.meaning: Where the anaesthetic was given, as one of the kinds of the location vocabulary.
columns.holds: The room or department of the theatre case or the anaesthetic record, whose kind the hospital's list of rooms or departments gives.

views.name: role_operation
views.title: Procedures done under an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each procedure done under an anaesthetic, so that an anaesthetic for several procedures has several rows, with the procedure as the local key of map_procedure_concept.
views.holds: The procedures of the theatre case or surgical log, with a lookup table of the procedures that the hospital offers.

columns.name: operation_key
columns.title: the operation's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the procedure line, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The procedure line's own key, which is often the theatre case and a line number.
look_for: unique id of the procedure line

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic under which the procedure was done, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The theatre case, which the anaesthetic record points at, or a link table between the two.

columns.name: procedure
columns.title: procedure
columns.meaning: The procedure, as the local key of map_procedure_concept, which gives its standard concept; the hospital's own code and name stay in the hospital schema.
columns.holds: The procedures of the theatre case, as a code that points at the hospital's list of procedures.

columns.name: specialty
columns.title: surgical specialty
columns.meaning: The surgical specialty of the procedure, as one of the kinds of the specialty vocabulary, which gives the operation's kind.
columns.holds: The service or specialty of the theatre case or of the surgeon.

columns.name: is_cardiac
columns.title: cardiac procedure
columns.meaning: 1 where the procedure was a cardiac operation or a cardiac catheter procedure, 0 where it was not, and empty where nothing says.
columns.holds: The specialty of the theatre case, the procedure's own code, or a diagnosis of the stay.

views.name: role_transfer
views.title: Transfers between units
views.description: One row for each transfer of a patient into or out of a unit during a hospital stay, as the source records it, so that a question works out the time spent in each unit, such as intensive care after an anaesthetic.
views.one_row_per: transfer into or out of a unit
views.holds: The movements of the encounter, with one row for each transfer in or out of a unit, and a lookup table that says what kind of unit each one is.

columns.name: transfer_key
columns.title: the transfer's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the transfer, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The movement row's own key.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay during which the transfer took place, as role_stay.stay_key.
columns.holds: The movement row.

columns.name: unit_kind
columns.title: kind of unit
columns.meaning: The kind of unit that the patient entered or left, as one of the kinds of the unit vocabulary.
columns.holds: The department or unit of the movement, whose kind the hospital's list of units gives.

columns.name: direction
columns.title: into or out of the unit
columns.meaning: Whether the patient entered or left the unit, as one of the kinds of the transfer direction vocabulary.
columns.holds: The movement row, as a code for the kind of movement, or as two rows of one movement, one for each unit.

columns.name: transfer_time
columns.title: time of the transfer
columns.meaning: When the patient entered or left the unit, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The movement row.

columns.name: source_kind
columns.title: kind of source record
columns.meaning: The kind of record from which the transfer came, as one of the kinds of the source kind vocabulary. The hospital schema names it for each pathway to this part, and the view gives it on every row of that pathway.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema names the kind of record of each pathway.

columns.name: documented_time
columns.title: time documented
columns.meaning: When the transfer was entered or filed, where the source records that apart from the time it describes, and empty where it does not.
columns.holds: The row itself, which often holds the time at which it was entered beside the time of what it records.

columns.name: amends_key
columns.title: the row it amends
columns.meaning: The key of the row of this part that this transfer amends or corrects, where the source records a correction as a row of its own, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The row itself, as a pointer to the row that it corrects or replaces.

views.name: role_event
views.title: Milestones of an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each timed milestone or complication of an anaesthetic, such as induction, intubation, incision, extubation, laryngospasm or arrival in recovery, with its kind from the event vocabulary.
views.holds: The events of the anaesthetic record or the timing events of the theatre case, each with a code for the kind of event; a complication may instead be held as a quality or incident record of the anaesthetic.

columns.name: event_key
columns.title: the event's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the event row, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The event row's own key, which is often the record and a line number.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic to which the event belongs, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key, where the source links the row to it, and empty where the source carries only the stay.
columns.holds: The event row, or the theatre case that it belongs to.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay of the event, as role_stay.stay_key, where the source carries it. A row whose source carries only the stay has this key and an empty anaesthetic_key, and a question attributes it to an anaesthetic by its own logic over the roles.
columns.holds: The row itself, or the encounter or order to which it belongs.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of milestone
columns.meaning: The kind of event, as one of the kinds of the event vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the event row with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: event_time
columns.title: time of the milestone
columns.meaning: When the event happened, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The event row.

columns.name: source_kind
columns.title: kind of source record
columns.meaning: The kind of record from which the event came, as one of the kinds of the source kind vocabulary. The hospital schema names it for each pathway to this part, and the view gives it on every row of that pathway.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema names the kind of record of each pathway.

columns.name: documented_time
columns.title: time documented
columns.meaning: When the event was entered or filed, where the source records that apart from the time it describes, and empty where it does not.
columns.holds: The row itself, which often holds the time at which it was entered beside the time of what it records.

columns.name: amends_key
columns.title: the row it amends
columns.meaning: The key of the row of this part that this event amends or corrects, where the source records a correction as a row of its own, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The row itself, as a pointer to the row that it corrects or replaces.

views.name: role_drug
views.title: Drugs given
views.description: One row for each dose given during an anaesthetic, and for each start, change of rate, pause, restart and stop of an infusion, as the source records it, with the drug as the local key of map_drug_concept.
views.holds: The administrations of the medication record, linked to their orders, or drug values charted on the anaesthetic record.

columns.name: drug_event_key
columns.title: the drug event's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the administration row, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The administration row's own key.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic to which the dose or infusion action belongs, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key, where the source links the row to it, and empty where the source carries only the stay.
columns.holds: The order of the drug, which belongs to the anaesthetic's own encounter, or the anaesthetic record on which the drug was charted.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay of the dose or infusion action, as role_stay.stay_key, where the source carries it. A row whose source carries only the stay has this key and an empty anaesthetic_key, and a question attributes it to an anaesthetic by its own logic over the roles.
columns.holds: The row itself, or the encounter or order to which it belongs.

columns.name: order_key
columns.title: the order's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the order that the dose or infusion action carries out, so that the start, rate changes, pauses and stop of one infusion can be told from those of another, and empty where the source records none.
columns.holds: The administration row, as the key of its order.

columns.name: drug
columns.title: drug
columns.meaning: The drug, as the local key of map_drug_concept, which gives its standard concept; the hospital's own code and name stay in the hospital schema.
columns.holds: The order, with a lookup table of the hospital's medications.

columns.name: action
columns.title: dose or infusion action
columns.meaning: What was done, as one of the kinds of the drug action vocabulary.
columns.holds: The administration row, as a code for the action.

columns.name: amount
columns.title: dose or rate
columns.meaning: The dose, or the rate of an infusion, as a number in the unit beside it, as the source records it.
columns.holds: The administration row.

columns.name: unit
columns.title: unit of the dose
columns.meaning: The unit of the amount, as the local key of map_unit_concept, which gives its standard concept.
columns.holds: The administration row, as a code for the unit.

columns.name: route
columns.title: route
columns.meaning: The route by which the drug was given, as one of the kinds of the route vocabulary.
columns.holds: The administration row or the order, as a code for the route with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: given_time
columns.title: time given
columns.meaning: When the dose was given or the infusion was started, changed, paused, restarted or stopped, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The administration row, which often holds a second time at which it was charted.
look_for: time that the action took place

columns.name: source_kind
columns.title: kind of source record
columns.meaning: The kind of record from which the dose or infusion action came, as one of the kinds of the source kind vocabulary. The hospital schema names it for each pathway to this part, and the view gives it on every row of that pathway.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema names the kind of record of each pathway.

columns.name: documented_time
columns.title: time documented
columns.meaning: When the dose or infusion action was entered or filed, where the source records that apart from the time it describes, and empty where it does not.
columns.holds: The row itself, which often holds the time at which it was entered beside the time of what it records.

columns.name: amends_key
columns.title: the row it amends
columns.meaning: The key of the row of this part that this dose or infusion action amends or corrects, where the source records a correction as a row of its own, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The row itself, as a pointer to the row that it corrects or replaces.

views.name: role_technique
views.title: Techniques of an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each technique charted for an anaesthetic, such as a general anaesthetic with an intravenous induction and a caudal block for one anaesthetic, as the record charts them.
views.holds: The anaesthetic record, usually as a list of the kinds of anaesthesia given, and a form or a procedure note for each block with its side, its guidance and any catheter.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic for which the technique was charted, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The list of techniques or the block's form, which belongs to the anaesthetic record or to its theatre case.

columns.name: technique_key
columns.title: the technique's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the charted technique, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The line of the list of techniques or the block's own form, which is often the anaesthetic and a line number.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of technique
columns.meaning: The technique, as one of the kinds of the technique vocabulary. An anaesthetic with several techniques has a row for each, and no row is chosen as the main one.
columns.holds: The anaesthetic record, usually as a code with a lookup table of names, and sometimes several for one anaesthetic.

columns.name: laterality
columns.title: side
columns.meaning: The side of the body on which a block was done, as one of the kinds of the laterality vocabulary, and empty for a technique that has no side.
columns.holds: The block's form, as a code for the side.

columns.name: guidance
columns.title: guidance
columns.meaning: How a block was guided, as one of the kinds of the guidance vocabulary, and empty for a technique that is not a block.
columns.holds: The block's form, as a code for the guidance used.

columns.name: catheter
columns.title: catheter left in place
columns.meaning: 1 where a catheter was left in place for the block, 0 where none was, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The block's form, or a device of the kind regional_catheter.

columns.name: recorded_time
columns.title: time of the technique
columns.meaning: When the technique was begun or the block was done, as the source holds it, and empty where the record gives no time.
columns.holds: The block's form or the list of techniques.

columns.name: documented_time
columns.title: time documented
columns.meaning: When the technique was entered or filed, where the source records that apart from the time of the technique, and empty where it does not.
columns.holds: The row itself, which often holds the time at which it was entered.

columns.name: performer
columns.title: the performer's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the staff member who did the technique, as role_staff.person_key gives it, and empty where the record does not say; never the person's name.
columns.holds: The block's form, as a key into the hospital's list of staff.

columns.name: source_kind
columns.title: kind of source record
columns.meaning: The kind of record from which the technique came, as one of the kinds of the source kind vocabulary. The hospital schema names it for each pathway to this part, and the view gives it on every row of that pathway.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema names the kind of record of each pathway.

columns.name: amends_key
columns.title: the row it amends
columns.meaning: The key of the row of this part that this technique amends or corrects, where the source records a correction as a row of its own, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The row itself, as a pointer to the row that it corrects or replaces.

views.name: role_fluid
views.title: Fluids and blood products
views.description: One row for each volume of fluid or blood product given during an anaesthetic, and for each volume of blood or urine lost, as the source charts it, whether as an amount or as a running total.
views.holds: The intake and output of the anaesthetic record, usually charted as measurements with a row for each kind of fluid, and the transfusion record for blood products.

columns.name: fluid_key
columns.title: the fluid's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the charted volume, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The charted value's own key, which is often the sheet and a line on it.
look_for: line of the intake or output

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic to which the fluid given or lost belongs, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key, where the source links the row to it, and empty where the source carries only the stay.
columns.holds: The sheet or record on which the volume was charted, or the order of the blood product.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay of the fluid given or lost, as role_stay.stay_key, where the source carries it. A row whose source carries only the stay has this key and an empty anaesthetic_key, and a question attributes it to an anaesthetic by its own logic over the roles.
columns.holds: The row itself, or the encounter or order to which it belongs.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of fluid
columns.meaning: What was given or lost, as one of the kinds of the fluid vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the row with a lookup table of names, or the product code of a blood product.

columns.name: volume_ml
columns.title: volume in millilitres
columns.meaning: The volume charted, in millilitres, as the source charts it: an amount, or a running total, as volume_form says.
columns.holds: The row itself, often as text.

columns.name: volume_form
columns.title: amount or running total
columns.meaning: Whether the volume is one amount or a running total since the start of the record, as one of the kinds of the volume form vocabulary; a question that wants amounts works them out from a running total.
columns.holds: The kind of row that the source charts, which the hospital schema names for each pathway, or a code on the row.

columns.name: given_time
columns.title: time given or measured
columns.meaning: When the volume was given or measured, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The row itself.

columns.name: source_kind
columns.title: kind of source record
columns.meaning: The kind of record from which the fluid given or lost came, as one of the kinds of the source kind vocabulary. The hospital schema names it for each pathway to this part, and the view gives it on every row of that pathway.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema names the kind of record of each pathway.

columns.name: documented_time
columns.title: time documented
columns.meaning: When the fluid given or lost was entered or filed, where the source records that apart from the time it describes, and empty where it does not.
columns.holds: The row itself, which often holds the time at which it was entered beside the time of what it records.

columns.name: amends_key
columns.title: the row it amends
columns.meaning: The key of the row of this part that this fluid given or lost amends or corrects, where the source records a correction as a row of its own, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The row itself, as a pointer to the row that it corrects or replaces.

views.name: role_device
views.title: Devices placed
views.description: One row for each airway device, line or catheter placed for an anaesthetic, with its kind from the device vocabulary.
views.holds: The lines, drains and airways of the patient's record, each with its placement and removal.

columns.name: device_key
columns.title: the device's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the device row, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The device row's own key.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic to which the device belongs, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key, where the source links the row to it, and empty where the source carries only the stay.
columns.holds: The device row, where it carries the anaesthetic's key; a device that belongs to the patient carries its stay.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay of the device, as role_stay.stay_key, where the source carries it. A row whose source carries only the stay has this key and an empty anaesthetic_key, and a question attributes it to an anaesthetic by its own logic over the roles.
columns.holds: The row itself, or the encounter or order to which it belongs.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of device
columns.meaning: The kind of device, as one of the kinds of the device vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the device row with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: placed_time
columns.title: time placed
columns.meaning: When the device was placed, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The device row.

columns.name: removed_time
columns.title: time removed
columns.meaning: When the device was removed, as the source holds it, and empty while it stays in place.
columns.holds: The device row.

columns.name: size
columns.title: size
columns.meaning: The size of the device as the hospital records it, such as the internal diameter of a tube or the gauge of a cannula.
columns.holds: The device row, or a property of the device charted as a measurement when it was placed.

columns.name: site
columns.title: site
columns.meaning: Where on the body the device was placed, as the hospital records it, such as the left radial artery or the right internal jugular vein.
columns.holds: The device row, often as a site and a side, or a property of the device charted when it was placed.

columns.name: source_kind
columns.title: kind of source record
columns.meaning: The kind of record from which the device came, as one of the kinds of the source kind vocabulary. The hospital schema names it for each pathway to this part, and the view gives it on every row of that pathway.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema names the kind of record of each pathway.

columns.name: documented_time
columns.title: time documented
columns.meaning: When the device was entered or filed, where the source records that apart from the time it describes, and empty where it does not.
columns.holds: The row itself, which often holds the time at which it was entered beside the time of what it records.

columns.name: amends_key
columns.title: the row it amends
columns.meaning: The key of the row of this part that this device amends or corrects, where the source records a correction as a row of its own, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The row itself, as a pointer to the row that it corrects or replaces.

views.name: role_staff
views.title: Staff attending an anaesthetic
views.description: One row for each person who attended an anaesthetic, for each period in which that person was present, with their role and grade.
views.holds: The staff or providers of the anaesthetic record or the theatre case, each with a role and a start and end of responsibility, and the hospital's list of staff for the grade.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic that the person attended, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key.
columns.holds: The staff row, or the theatre case that it belongs to.

columns.name: person_key
columns.title: the staff member's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the staff member, and never the person's name.
columns.holds: The staff row, as a key into the hospital's list of staff.
look_for: unique id of the staff member

columns.name: role
columns.title: role at the anaesthetic
columns.meaning: What the person did at the anaesthetic, as one of the kinds of the staff role vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the staff row with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: grade
columns.title: grade
columns.meaning: The person's grade at the time of the anaesthetic, as one of the kinds of the grade vocabulary.
columns.holds: The hospital's list of staff, as a provider type or a title; that list usually holds the grade today, and not the grade on the day.

columns.name: present_from
columns.title: time of joining
columns.meaning: When the person took over or joined the care of the patient, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The staff row.
look_for: start time of the staff member

columns.name: present_to
columns.title: time of leaving
columns.meaning: When the person handed over or left the care of the patient, as the source holds it, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The staff row.
look_for: end time of the staff member

views.name: role_lab
views.title: Laboratory results
views.description: One row for each laboratory or point-of-care result for the patient, linked to the patient and the stay rather than to an anaesthetic.
views.holds: The results of the laboratory's orders, with one row for each component of each result, and the point-of-care and blood gas results that the hospital files with them.

columns.name: lab_key
columns.title: the result's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the result component, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The result component's own key, which is often the order and a line number.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient whose result it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The order of the test, or the encounter to which it belongs.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay during which the specimen was taken, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty where the result belongs to no stay.
columns.holds: The order of the test, which points at an encounter that is the stay or belongs to it.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of test
columns.meaning: What was measured, as one of the kinds of the laboratory vocabulary.
columns.holds: A code on the result for its component or test, with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: test
columns.title: test
columns.meaning: The test or component, as the local key of map_lab_concept, which gives its standard concept, so that a result of the kind other can still be told apart; the hospital's own code and name stay in the hospital schema.
columns.holds: A code on the result for its component or test, with a lookup table of names.

columns.name: value
columns.title: result
columns.meaning: The result as a number in the kind's own unit, which the view converts to where the hospital holds another, and empty where the result is not a number.
columns.holds: The result row, often both as text and as a number.

columns.name: unit
columns.title: unit of the result
columns.meaning: The unit in which the hospital recorded the result, as the local key of map_unit_concept, so that a person can check the conversion.
columns.holds: The result row or the component's lookup table.

columns.name: taken_time
columns.title: time the specimen was taken
columns.meaning: When the specimen was taken, as the source holds it, and not when the result was reported.
columns.holds: The result row or the specimen, which often hold the times of collection, receipt and result.

columns.name: source_kind
columns.title: kind of source record
columns.meaning: The kind of record from which the result came, as one of the kinds of the source kind vocabulary. The hospital schema names it for each pathway to this part, and the view gives it on every row of that pathway.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema names the kind of record of each pathway.

columns.name: documented_time
columns.title: time documented
columns.meaning: When the result was entered or filed, where the source records that apart from the time it describes, and empty where it does not.
columns.holds: The row itself, which often holds the time at which it was entered beside the time of what it records.

columns.name: amends_key
columns.title: the row it amends
columns.meaning: The key of the row of this part that this result amends or corrects, where the source records a correction as a row of its own, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The row itself, as a pointer to the row that it corrects or replaces.

views.name: role_diagnosis
views.title: Coded diagnoses
views.description: One row for each coded diagnosis of the patient, from the coded discharge diagnoses, the problem list or the indication on the theatre booking, with the diagnosis as the local key of map_diagnosis_concept.
views.holds: The coded diagnoses of the encounter or the hospital account, the patient's problem list, and the indication or diagnosis on the theatre booking, each with a lookup table of diagnoses.

columns.name: diagnosis_key
columns.title: the diagnosis's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the diagnosis row, or, where the record has none, a value that the map makes from the columns that identify a row, unique to each row; the map says which.
columns.holds: The diagnosis row's own key, which is often the encounter and a line number.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient whose diagnosis it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The diagnosis row, or the encounter or problem list to which it belongs.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay for which the diagnosis was coded, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty for a problem-list entry that belongs to no stay.
columns.holds: The diagnosis row, as the key of the encounter or of the hospital account that belongs to the stay.

columns.name: diagnosis
columns.title: diagnosis
columns.meaning: The diagnosis, as the local key of map_diagnosis_concept, which gives its standard concept; the hospital's own code, classification and name stay in the hospital schema.
columns.holds: The lookup table of diagnoses, which the diagnosis row points at, or the diagnosis row itself.

columns.name: is_principal
columns.title: principal diagnosis
columns.meaning: 1 where the diagnosis is the principal diagnosis of the stay, 0 where it is another, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: A flag or a sequence number on the diagnosis row, where the first line is the principal one.

columns.name: recorded_time
columns.title: time recorded
columns.meaning: When the diagnosis was noted or coded, as the source holds it, and empty where the record does not say.
columns.holds: The diagnosis row or the problem-list entry, as the date noted or the date of entry.

columns.name: source_kind
columns.title: kind of source record
columns.meaning: The kind of record from which the diagnosis came, as one of the kinds of the source kind vocabulary. The hospital schema names it for each pathway to this part, and the view gives it on every row of that pathway.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema names the kind of record of each pathway.

columns.name: documented_time
columns.title: time documented
columns.meaning: When the diagnosis was entered or filed, where the source records that apart from the time it describes, and empty where it does not.
columns.holds: The row itself, which often holds the time at which it was entered beside the time of what it records.

columns.name: amends_key
columns.title: the row it amends
columns.meaning: The key of the row of this part that this diagnosis amends or corrects, where the source records a correction as a row of its own, and empty otherwise.
columns.holds: The row itself, as a pointer to the row that it corrects or replaces.

views.name: role_note
views.title: Notes in the record
views.description: One row for each piece of free text in the record, such as a pre-anaesthetic assessment or an anaesthetic summary, with its text joined back into one value. A query that returns its text is an extract of identifying detail, and never a count.
views.holds: A notes table keyed by encounter with a note type, whose text is often split across several rows that the view joins back in order, and sometimes the comment fields of a structured form.

columns.name: note_key
columns.title: the note's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital's own identifier of the note, the same value that role_finding.note_key holds.
columns.holds: The note's own key, or the key of the form whose comment field holds the text.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic to which the note belongs, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key, and empty where the system makes no link to one.
columns.holds: The note row, where it carries the anaesthetic's key or the key of the anaesthetic's own encounter.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient whose note it is, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The note row, or the encounter to which it belongs.

columns.name: stay_key
columns.title: the stay's identifier
columns.meaning: The hospital stay to which the note belongs, as role_stay.stay_key, and empty where it belongs to no stay, such as a note of a clinic visit.
columns.holds: The note row, as the key of its encounter.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of note
columns.meaning: What kind of note it is, as one of the kinds of the note vocabulary.
columns.holds: A note type on the note row, with a lookup table of names that the hospital builds.

columns.name: written_time
columns.title: time written
columns.meaning: When the note was written or signed, as the source holds it, and not when it was last edited.
columns.holds: The note row, which often holds the times of creation, signing and each edit.

columns.name: author_role
columns.title: author's grade
columns.meaning: The grade of the person who wrote the note, as one of the kinds of the grade vocabulary.
columns.holds: The author's provider type on the note row, or the hospital's list of staff.

columns.name: text
columns.title: text of the note
columns.meaning: The whole text of the note, with its lines joined back in order.
columns.holds: The lines of the note's text, each a row with a line number, or a single long text field.

views.name: role_finding
views.title: Facts found in the record
views.description: One row for each fact that the hospital's own process takes from a note or from a structured field, such as a Mallampati grade or the hours of fasting, with how it was found.
views.holds: The discrete answers of a structured pre-anaesthetic assessment or anaesthetic summary, which a map should find first, and otherwise a table that the hospital fills from its notes by rules, by a person or by a model run inside the hospital.

columns.name: note_key
columns.title: the note's identifier
columns.meaning: The note from which the fact was taken, as role_note.note_key, and empty for a fact taken from a structured field.
columns.holds: The answer row or the hospital's own table of findings.

columns.name: anaesthetic_key
columns.title: the anaesthetic's identifier
columns.meaning: The anaesthetic to which the fact belongs, as role_anaesthetic.anaesthetic_key, and empty where nothing links it to one.
columns.holds: The answer row, or the note from which the fact was taken.

columns.name: patient_key
columns.title: the patient's identifier
columns.meaning: The patient of whom the fact is true, as role_patient.patient_key.
columns.holds: The answer row, or the note or encounter to which it belongs.

columns.name: kind
columns.title: kind of fact
columns.meaning: What the fact is about, as one of the kinds of the finding vocabulary.
columns.holds: The question or element that the answer belongs to, with a lookup table of names that the hospital builds.

columns.name: value
columns.title: value of the fact
columns.meaning: The fact as text, such as 3 for a Mallampati grade, 6 for the hours of fasting, or yes or no for a history.
columns.holds: The answer row, often as text that holds numbers and words alike.

columns.name: method
columns.title: method of finding
columns.meaning: How the fact was found, as one of the kinds of the finding method vocabulary.
columns.holds: A fixed value for each source that the map reads, such as structured_field for the answers of a form.

columns.name: confidence
columns.title: confidence
columns.meaning: The confidence that the hospital's process gives the fact, from 0 to 1, and empty where it gives none, as for a structured field or a person's reading.
columns.holds: The hospital's own table of findings, where a rule or a model fills it.

columns.name: found_time
columns.title: time found
columns.meaning: When the fact was recorded in a structured field, or taken from the note, as the source holds it.
columns.holds: The answer row, or the hospital's own table of findings.

types.key: Any type that compares equal with itself within one hospital, such as a whole number or text.
types.datetime: A date and a time of day, as the source holds it.
types.number: A number that may hold a fraction.
types.flag: The whole number 1 or 0, and never empty.
types.flag_or_empty: The whole number 1 or 0, or empty where the record does not say.
types.kind: Text that is one of the kinds of the vocabulary that the column names.
types.text: Text as the hospital records it.
types.local_key: Opaque text that is the local key of a row of the mapping view that the column names, made by the hospital schema from the hospital's own code and never the code itself.

kinds.meaning: A mean arterial pressure from an arterial line, in mmHg.
A mean arterial pressure from a non-invasive cuff, in mmHg.
A heart rate, in beats a minute.
An oxygen saturation by pulse oximetry, in per cent.
An end-tidal carbon dioxide, in mmHg.
A body temperature, in degrees Celsius.
A systolic pressure from an arterial line, in mmHg.
A diastolic pressure from an arterial line, in mmHg.
A systolic pressure from a non-invasive cuff, in mmHg.
A diastolic pressure from a non-invasive cuff, in mmHg.
A central venous pressure, in mmHg.
A fraction of inspired oxygen, in per cent.
A positive end-expiratory pressure, in cmH2O.
An expired tidal volume, in millilitres.
A respiratory rate, in breaths a minute.
An end-tidal concentration of a volatile agent, in per cent, whichever agent it is.
A pain score, as a number on the scale that the hospital uses, usually from 0 to 10.
A blood glucose charted in the anaesthetic's record, usually from a bedside meter, in mmol/L.
The total fresh gas flow, in litres a minute.
An inspired concentration of sevoflurane, in per cent.
An expired concentration of sevoflurane, in per cent.
An inspired concentration of desflurane, in per cent.
An expired concentration of desflurane, in per cent.
An inspired concentration of isoflurane, in per cent.
An expired concentration of isoflurane, in per cent.
An inspired concentration of nitrous oxide, in per cent.
A peak airway pressure, in cmH2O.
A plateau pressure, in cmH2O.
The mode of ventilation, which is not a number and is kept as charted in value_text.
A pain score on the FLACC scale, from 0 to 10.
A pain score on a numeric rating scale, from 0 to 10.
A pain score on the Wong-Baker faces scale, from 0 to 10.
A score of nausea and vomiting, on the scale that the chart uses.
A sedation score, on the scale that the chart uses.
A score of the Child Induction Behavioral Assessment.
A score of the Paediatric Anaesthesia Emergence Delirium scale.
Any other value charted in the anaesthetic's record, which the counts use to see whether the record is reached at all.

sex.meaning: Any other value, or one that says nothing was recorded.

technique.meaning: A general anaesthetic with an inhalational induction.
A general anaesthetic with an intravenous induction.
Sedation given by an anaesthetist, including monitored anaesthesia care.
A block of the brachial plexus or of a nerve of the arm.
A block of the femoral, sciatic or another nerve of the leg, including a fascia iliaca block.
A block of the trunk, such as a transversus abdominis plane, rectus sheath, erector spinae or paravertebral block.
An ilioinguinal, iliohypogastric or penile block.
A block of the scalp, the face or the neck.
Local anaesthetic infiltrated at the site of surgery by the anaesthetist.
Any other technique, or one that the record does not give.

specialty.meaning: Cardiac surgery and cardiac catheter procedures.
Imaging and other procedures outside theatre.

unit.meaning: An intensive care unit, neonatal, paediatric or adult.
An operating theatre or a procedure room.

location.meaning: A radiology or imaging suite, such as for MRI or CT.
A cardiac or interventional catheter laboratory.
An intensive care unit, neonatal, paediatric or adult.
A ward or a procedure room on a ward.
Any other place, such as an endoscopy or oncology procedure room.

event.meaning: The airway placed or the trachea intubated.
A fall in oxygen saturation that the record marks as an event or complication.
A difficult mask ventilation, laryngoscopy or intubation recorded as such.
A cardiac arrest, or chest compressions started.
A drug error recorded against the anaesthetic.
A block that failed or was inadequate, as the record marks it.
A regional technique or sedation converted to a general anaesthetic.
A complication of a block, such as a vascular puncture, local anaesthetic toxicity or a nerve injury, as the record marks it.

device.meaning: A laryngeal mask or other supraglottic airway.
An epidural or other regional catheter.

drug_action.meaning: A dose or an infusion ordered, before any is given.
The rate of an infusion changed.
An infusion paused, to be restarted.
A dose that was charted but not given.

note.meaning: A pre-anaesthetic assessment, in a clinic, on the ward or on the day.
The anaesthetist's summary or record of the anaesthetic.
A note of the airway, such as of a difficult intubation, or an airway alert.
A note of a procedure done by the anaesthetist, such as a block or a central line.
The discharge summary of the stay.
A progress note on the ward or in intensive care.

finding.meaning: A difficult airway known or found, such as a difficult intubation at a previous anaesthetic.
The hours since the last solids or fluids, as the note gives them.
A problem at a previous anaesthetic.
A family history of a problem with anaesthesia, such as malignant hyperthermia or suxamethonium apnoea.
A named syndrome or genetic condition.
A cardiac history, such as congenital heart disease.
A respiratory history, such as asthma or prematurity with chronic lung disease.
A recent upper respiratory tract infection.
An allergy, as the note or the form gives it.

finding_method.meaning: Read from a discrete answer of a structured form.
Found by a pattern query over role_note that was tested on invented notes.
Found by a person reading the note.
Found by a model that the hospital chose to run inside the hospital.

staff_role.meaning: A surgeon or proceduralist, of any grade.
An anaesthetic nurse or anaesthetic technician who assisted the anaesthetist.
Any other person present, such as a scrub or scout nurse, a perfusionist or a student.

grade.meaning: A fellow, or a provisional fellow in the last year of training.
A registrar or other trainee in a specialty programme.
A resident medical officer or intern who is not in a specialty programme.
A nurse, including a nurse practitioner.
Any other grade, such as a technician or a student, or one that the record does not give.

fluid.meaning: A crystalloid, such as a balanced salt solution, saline or a dextrose solution.
A colloid, such as albumin or a starch or gelatin solution.
Fresh frozen plasma or another plasma product.
Blood salvaged from the operative field and returned to the patient.
Blood lost, as measured or estimated.
Any other fluid given or lost, such as a drain's output or a gastric aspirate.

lab.meaning: A glucose measured by the laboratory or a blood gas analyser, in mmol/L.
A pH, which has no unit.
A partial pressure of carbon dioxide, in mmHg.
A partial pressure of oxygen, in mmHg.
Any other result, in the unit beside it.

laterality.meaning: The midline, as for a caudal or a neuraxial block.

guidance.meaning: Guided by ultrasound, with or without a nerve stimulator.
Guided by a nerve stimulator without ultrasound.
The record says that no guidance was used.

route.meaning: On the skin or a mucous membrane.
Infiltrated into the tissues at the site of surgery.
Around a nerve or plexus, for a peripheral block.
Any other route, or one that the record does not give.

volume_form.meaning: One amount given or lost at the time charted.
The total given or lost since the start of the record, up to the time charted.

source_kind.meaning: An order or a prescription, made before anything is done.
A record that a drug or a fluid was given, made by the person who gave it.
A value charted on the anaesthetic record or a flowsheet, by hand or from a device.
A log of the case, such as the timing events or the procedures of the theatre case.
A record of a line, an airway or another device, with its placement and removal.
A movement of the patient into or out of a unit.
A result reported by the laboratory or by a point-of-care analyser.
A code assigned after the event, as at discharge.
An entry of the patient's problem list.
A booking or request made before the event, such as the indication on a theatre booking.
An incident or quality record made about the event.
A row that the source records to amend or correct an earlier row.

mapping_status.meaning: The local code means one standard concept.
No standard concept has been chosen for the local code, and the concept is 0.
The local code may mean more than one standard concept, and the view gives a row for each.

mapping_provenance.meaning: A person who knows the hospital's codes chose the concept.
A conversion written at another hospital gave the concept.
The hospital's own conversion to OMOP gave the concept.
The concept was proposed by matching words, and no person has confirmed it.

mapping_views.name: map_drug_concept
mapping_views.title: Drugs
mapping_views.description: One row for each local code of drugs that the hospital schema knows and each standard concept it may mean: one row where the code is mapped or unmapped, and a row for each candidate where it is ambiguous.

columns.name: local_key
columns.title: the local key
columns.meaning: An opaque key that the hospital schema makes from the hospital's own code, the same value that the part's column holds; it is never the code itself.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema makes it from the code.

columns.name: concept_id
columns.title: the standard concept
columns.meaning: The concept that the local code means, which is a standard concept of OMOP's Drug domain, such as an ingredient or a clinical drug, and 0 where the status is unmapped.
columns.holds: The hospital schema's translation of the code, chosen by a person or taken from a conversion.

columns.name: status
columns.title: the mapping's status
columns.meaning: Whether the local code is mapped, unmapped or ambiguous, as one of the kinds of the mapping status vocabulary.
columns.holds: The hospital schema's translation of the code.

columns.name: provenance
columns.title: where the mapping came from
columns.meaning: Where the mapping came from, as one of the kinds of the mapping provenance vocabulary.
columns.holds: The hospital schema's translation of the code.

mapping_views.name: map_procedure_concept
mapping_views.title: Procedures
mapping_views.description: One row for each local code of procedures that the hospital schema knows and each standard concept it may mean: one row where the code is mapped or unmapped, and a row for each candidate where it is ambiguous.

columns.name: local_key
columns.title: the local key
columns.meaning: An opaque key that the hospital schema makes from the hospital's own code, the same value that the part's column holds; it is never the code itself.
columns.holds: Nothing in the hospital's tables: the hospital schema makes it from the code.

columns.name: concept_id
columns.title: the standard concept
columns.meaning: The concept that the local code means, which is a standard concept of OMOP's Procedure domain, and 0 where the status is unmapped.
columns.holds: The hospital schema's translation of the code, chosen by a person or taken from a conversion.

columns.name: status
columns.title: the mapping's status
columns.meaning: Whether the local code is mapped, unmapped or ambiguous, as one of the kinds of the mapping status vocabulary.
columns.holds: The hospital schema's translation of the code.

columns.name: provenance
columns.title: where the mapping came from
columns.meaning: Where the mapping came from, as one of the kinds of the mapping provenance vocabulary.
columns.holds: The hospital schema's translation of the code.

mapping_views.name: map_diagnosis_concept

output_classes.meaning: A row for each anaesthetic, with the value the capability measures.
A count or another figure over many anaesthetics, rounded where it leaves the hospital.
A row for each anaesthetic, with 1 where the capability holds and 0 where it does not.

capabilities.name: death_within_days
capabilities.meaning: Whether the patient died within a given number of days of the anaesthetic's start, counted by calendar date.

parameters.name: days
parameters.meaning: How many days after the day of the anaesthetic's start count.

capabilities.window: from the day of the start to the given number of days after it

capabilities.name: unplanned_intensive_care
capabilities.meaning: Whether the patient entered intensive care within 24 hours after the anaesthetic's stop, when intensive care had not been planned and the patient was not already there at the start.
capabilities.window: the 24 hours after the anaesthetic's stop

capabilities.name: return_to_theatre_30_days
capabilities.meaning: Whether the same patient had another anaesthetic with an operation within 30 days after this one's stop, and whether the hospital recorded that return as unplanned.
capabilities.window: the 30 days after the anaesthetic's stop

capabilities.name: length_of_stay
capabilities.meaning: The time from admission to discharge of the stay in which the anaesthetic took place, and the time from the anaesthetic's stop to that discharge.

capabilities.name: readmission_30_days
capabilities.meaning: Whether the patient began another unplanned stay within 30 days after the discharge of the stay in which the anaesthetic took place.
capabilities.window: the 30 days after the stay's discharge

capabilities.name: anaesthetic_complication
capabilities.meaning: Whether the anaesthetic's record holds any of the complications of the event vocabulary, such as laryngospasm, desaturation or cardiac arrest.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.meaning: The complications of the event vocabulary that count.

capabilities.name: transfusion
capabilities.meaning: Whether the patient was given red cells, platelets, plasma or cryoprecipitate during the anaesthetic, and how much in millilitres for each kilogram.

capabilities.name: recovery_time
capabilities.meaning: The time from arrival in recovery to discharge from recovery.

capabilities.name: postoperative_result
capabilities.meaning: A laboratory result, such as a lactate or a creatinine, in a window after the anaesthetic's stop that the audit chooses.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.meaning: The kind of laboratory result.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.meaning: How long after the stop the window runs.

capabilities.window: a number of hours after the anaesthetic's stop

capabilities.name: gestational_age
capabilities.meaning: The gestational age at birth, as recorded.

capabilities.name: weight_at_anaesthetic
capabilities.meaning: The patient's weight at the anaesthetic, as recorded.

capabilities.name: asa_grade
capabilities.meaning: The ASA physical status grade, as recorded.

capabilities.name: emergency
capabilities.meaning: Whether the operation was done as an emergency, as recorded.

capabilities.name: cardiac
capabilities.meaning: Whether any procedure under the anaesthetic was cardiac.

capabilities.name: operation_kind
capabilities.meaning: The specialty of the main procedure, which the audit chooses by its own rule.

capabilities.name: height_at_anaesthetic
capabilities.meaning: The patient's height or length at the anaesthetic, as recorded.

capabilities.name: location
capabilities.meaning: Where the anaesthetic was given, as recorded.

capabilities.name: consultant_present
capabilities.meaning: Whether an anaesthetist of the grade consultant was present at any time during the anaesthetic.

capabilities.name: principal_diagnosis
capabilities.meaning: The principal diagnosis of the stay in which the anaesthetic took place, as a standard concept.

capabilities.name: preoperative_result
capabilities.meaning: A laboratory result, such as a haemoglobin, in a window before the anaesthetic's start that the audit chooses.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.meaning: The kind of laboratory result.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.meaning: How long before the start the window runs.

capabilities.window: a number of hours before the anaesthetic's start

capabilities.name: assessment_finding
capabilities.meaning: A fact from the assessment, such as a recent upper respiratory tract infection or snoring, which the audit may restrict to the methods that it trusts.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.meaning: The kind of finding.

parameters.name: methods
parameters.meaning: The methods of finding that the audit trusts.

capabilities.name: minutes_beyond_threshold
capabilities.meaning: The minutes of an anaesthetic during which accepted readings of a kind lay beyond a threshold, counting each reading until the next.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.meaning: The kind of reading.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.meaning: Below or above the threshold.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.meaning: The threshold.

parameters.name: window
parameters.meaning: The part of the anaesthetic over which the minutes are counted.

capabilities.window: from the anaesthetic's start to its stop

capabilities.name: extreme_in_window
capabilities.meaning: The lowest or highest accepted reading of a kind within a window relative to the anaesthetic.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.meaning: The kind of reading.

parameters.name: extreme
parameters.meaning: The lowest or the highest.

parameters.name: window
parameters.meaning: The part of the anaesthetic over which the extreme is found.

capabilities.window: from the anaesthetic's start to its stop

capabilities.name: time_to_first_beyond_threshold
capabilities.meaning: The minutes from the anaesthetic's start to the first accepted reading of a kind beyond a threshold, and empty where none lies beyond it.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.meaning: The kind of reading.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.meaning: Below or above the threshold.

parameters.name: threshold
parameters.meaning: The threshold.

capabilities.window: from the anaesthetic's start to its stop

capabilities.name: count_of_events
capabilities.meaning: How many events of the chosen kinds the anaesthetic's record holds within a window.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.meaning: The kinds of event that count.

parameters.name: window
parameters.meaning: The part of the anaesthetic over which events are counted.

capabilities.name: total_volume_per_kg
capabilities.meaning: The total volume of the chosen kinds of fluid given during the anaesthetic, for each kilogram of the patient's weight, with running totals turned into amounts.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.meaning: The kinds of fluid that count.

capabilities.name: exposure_intervals
capabilities.meaning: The intervals during which an infusion of a drug ran, from its start, rate changes, pauses, restarts and stop, with an interval whose stop the source does not record kept as one of unknown end.

parameters.name: drugs
parameters.meaning: The standard concepts of the drugs whose infusions count.

capabilities.grain: one row for each interval of an infusion

capabilities.name: hypotension_burden
capabilities.meaning: The minutes of an anaesthetic, within a window, during which accepted readings of the chosen pressure kinds lay beyond a threshold set by the patient's age, counting each reading until the next and for no longer than a set time.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.meaning: The kinds of reading that count, each with its preference: where readings of two kinds share a time, the kind with the lower preference is kept.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.meaning: Below or above the threshold.

parameters.name: threshold_by_age_band
parameters.meaning: The threshold for each band of the patient's age in days at the start, counted by calendar date from the date of birth, from from_days up to but not including until_days, which is empty for no limit.

parameters.name: window_from_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window begins, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start.

parameters.name: window_until_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window ends, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start, or empty for its stop; the window never runs past a recorded stop.

parameters.name: reading_stands_minutes
parameters.meaning: The longest time for which one reading stands.

capabilities.window: from window_from_minutes after the anaesthetic's start to window_until_minutes after it, or to its stop

capabilities.name: hypoxaemia_burden
capabilities.meaning: The minutes of an anaesthetic, within a window, during which accepted readings of saturation lay below a threshold set by the patient's age, counting each reading until the next and for no longer than a set time.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.meaning: The kinds of reading that count, each with its preference: where readings of two kinds share a time, the kind with the lower preference is kept.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.meaning: Below or above the threshold.

parameters.name: threshold_by_age_band
parameters.meaning: The threshold for each band of the patient's age in days at the start, counted by calendar date from the date of birth, from from_days up to but not including until_days, which is empty for no limit.

parameters.name: window_from_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window begins, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start.

parameters.name: window_until_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window ends, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start, or empty for its stop; the window never runs past a recorded stop.

parameters.name: reading_stands_minutes
parameters.meaning: The longest time for which one reading stands.

capabilities.window: from window_from_minutes after the anaesthetic's start to window_until_minutes after it, or to its stop

capabilities.name: hypothermia
capabilities.meaning: The minutes of an anaesthetic, within a window, during which accepted temperatures lay below a threshold, the lowest temperature in the window, and the first temperature after the anaesthetic's stop, within a recovery window anchored to the stop, as the temperature on arrival in recovery.

parameters.name: threshold_celsius
parameters.meaning: The threshold below which the minutes are counted.

parameters.name: window_from_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window begins, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start.

parameters.name: window_until_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window ends, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start, or empty for its stop; the window never runs past a recorded stop.

parameters.name: reading_stands_minutes
parameters.meaning: The longest time for which one reading stands.

parameters.name: recovery_window_minutes
parameters.meaning: How long after the anaesthetic's stop a temperature still counts as the one taken on arrival in recovery.

capabilities.window: from window_from_minutes after the anaesthetic's start to window_until_minutes after it, or to its stop, and for the arrival, from just after the stop to recovery_window_minutes after it

capabilities.name: monitoring_completeness
capabilities.meaning: The share of a window that lies within an expected interval after an accepted reading of the chosen kinds, and the longest gap in the window without one.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.meaning: The kinds of reading that count, any of which covers the window.

parameters.name: expected_interval_minutes
parameters.meaning: How long after a reading the window counts as covered.

parameters.name: window_from_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window begins, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start.

parameters.name: window_until_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window ends, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start, or empty for its stop; the window never runs past a recorded stop.

capabilities.unit: a share of the window, and minutes
capabilities.window: from window_from_minutes after the anaesthetic's start to window_until_minutes after it, or to its stop

capabilities.name: volatile_consumption
capabilities.meaning: The millilitres of liquid volatile agent consumed in an anaesthetic, for each agent, from the fresh gas flow and the expired concentration integrated over time, with the carbon dioxide equivalent from a factor for each agent.

parameters.name: vapour_per_liquid
parameters.meaning: The expired concentration's kind of each agent that counts, with its millilitres of vapour for each millilitre of liquid.

parameters.name: co2e_per_liquid
parameters.meaning: The kilograms of carbon dioxide equivalent for each millilitre of each agent's liquid.

parameters.name: reading_stands_minutes
parameters.meaning: The longest time for which one reading stands.

parameters.name: window_from_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window begins, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start.

parameters.name: window_until_minutes
parameters.meaning: Where the window ends, in minutes after the anaesthetic's start, or empty for its stop; the window never runs past a recorded stop.

capabilities.grain: one row for each anaesthetic and agent
capabilities.unit: mL of liquid, and kg of carbon dioxide equivalent
capabilities.window: from window_from_minutes after the anaesthetic's start to window_until_minutes after it, or to its stop
